content.user_title: Analyze Stocks With Graham and Buffett Frameworks
content.value_statement: Value investors need disciplined checks across price, quality, and statement consistency. This skill guides Graham and Buffett analysis with Longbridge data and source appendices.
actual_capabilities: Routes requests to Graham single-stock, Graham screener, Buffett moat analyzer, or Buffett screener workflows.
Uses Longbridge CLI first, MCP fallback when available, and WebSearch only for documented data gaps.
Applies NCAV, PE, PB, dividends, debt coverage, earnings stability, and value-trap checks.
Scores Buffett candidates with moat, financial health, management, valuation, and long-term visibility dimensions.
Runs cross-statement reconciliation before scoring and flags data mismatches above thresholds.
Requires a data source appendix for Longbridge endpoints, WebSearch sources, fetch times, and periods.
limitations: Does not provide personal investment advice or buy and sell recommendations.
Depends on Longbridge CLI, MCP, or WebSearch availability for current data.
Financial sectors and early-stage companies may use adjusted rules or exclusions.
Screening results depend on the selected universe and supported market data.

use_cases.title: Check a Deep-Value Candidate
use_cases.description: Evaluate one stock with Graham NCAV, valuation, dividend, debt, earnings stability, and value-trap checks.

use_cases.title: Screen a Market Universe
use_cases.description: Create a ranked list of Graham net-net or Buffett quality candidates with exclusions and data notes.

use_cases.title: Compare Moat Quality
use_cases.description: Review business quality, financial health, management, valuation, and long-term visibility for portfolio candidates.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One Stock
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze 00700.HK using the Buffett moat framework. Show the required data source appendix.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Graham Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate 600519.SH with Graham NCAV, PE, PB, dividend, debt coverage, and value-trap checks.

prompt_templates.title: Screen for Net-Nets
prompt_templates.prompt: Screen the Hong Kong market for Graham net-net candidates. Rank by adjusted cigar-butt score and flag exclusions.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Quality Compounder Shortlist
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Buffett-style consumer stocks in the US market. Apply hard filters, moat scoring, valuation tiers, and holding-period guidance.

output: Five-dimension moat card with star ratings and a minimum holding-period view.
Evidence sections for moat, financial health, management, valuation, and long-term visibility.
Data source appendix with Longbridge data rows and reconciliation summary.

output_examples.input: Graham net-net screen for Hong Kong stocks
output: Ranked candidate list with NCAV ratio, PE, PB, dividend yield, Graham buy price, and warning flags.
Market summary that counts the universe, hard-filter pass rate, exclusions, and data anomalies.
Source appendix for each Longbridge endpoint and any WebSearch fallback.

output_examples.input: Graham analysis for a stock with inconsistent statements
output: Halt message naming the failed reconciliation check and the affected figures.
No score is emitted until the data issue is resolved.
Appendix still lists sources, periods, and the failed check.

best_practices: Give a ticker and market suffix when possible.
State the preferred framework and investment horizon.
Review the data source appendix before comparing scores.
anti_patterns: Treating the output as personal financial advice.
Mixing Longbridge and WebSearch figures without source labels.
Forcing Buffett scoring on pre-revenue or history-limited companies.

faq.question: Does this skill give investment advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured research and source-tagged analysis for informational use.

faq.question: Which data sources does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Longbridge first, MCP as a fallback, and WebSearch only for documented gaps.

faq.question: What is the difference between Graham and Buffett modes?
faq.answer: Graham mode focuses on asset value and cheapness. Buffett mode focuses on business quality, moat, and fair valuation.

faq.question: Can it screen a full market?
faq.answer: Yes. It can screen a selected market or sector, subject to data availability and batch limits.

faq.question: Why does it run reconciliation checks?
faq.answer: The checks compare financial statements before scoring. Large mismatches halt or remove affected results.

faq.question: Which languages are supported?
faq.answer: The skill is designed to respond in English, Simplified Chinese, or Traditional Chinese based on the user prompt.
